Statistical process control (SPC) charts track process outputs over time to identify common and special cause variations.
Pareto analysis applies the 80/20 rule to identify the vital few root causes that contribute to the majority of defects.
Root cause analysis penetrates beyond surface symptoms to determine the fundamental reasons behind operational or financial variances.
Management investigates a variance when it exceeds a established materiality threshold in terms of percentage or dollar amount.
Favorable variances can result from efficient operations or negative issues such as loose standards, inferior materials, or reduced quality.
Decisions to investigate variances depend on materiality of the amount, controllability of the cause, and persistence of the trend.
Segment margin is segment revenue less direct costs and traceable fixed costs, ignoring allocated common fixed costs.
Common fixed costs remain unchanged regardless of whether a specific segment is kept or dropped and are therefore irrelevant.
A business segment should be eliminated if the cost savings (avoidable costs) exceed the contribution margin lost by dropping it.
The Balanced Scorecard establishes operational balance by combining traditional financial indicators with non-financial drivers.
Leading indicators measure intermediate activities that drive future operational and financial performance outcomes.
Lagging indicators represent end-result performance measures that reflect past achievements and consequences.
Market share directly assesses customer acquisition and competitive position within the customer perspective.
Employee turnover measures human capital retention within the learning and growth perspective of the Balanced Scorecard.
Cycle time evaluates operational speed and efficiency, making it an internal business process perspective measure.
First-pass yield measures manufacturing process quality and efficiency under internal business processes.

Budget-to-actual variance analysis assesses monetary performance under the financial perspective.
Customer satisfaction surveys quantify customer perception regarding product/service quality, performance, and value.
Target costing achieves maximum effectiveness during initial product design and development when manufacturing costs are largely locked in.
Value engineering systematically examines product functions and components to lower costs while maintaining required functionality and quality.
A cost allocation base should reflect a cause-and-effect relationship between the base and the costs being allocated.
A cost driver is a factor that causes changes in the level of cost, such as machine hours or number of setups.
Traditional costing systems typically use volume-based cost drivers such as direct labor hours or machine hours.
ABC provides more accurate costing when overhead costs are large and diverse, as it uses multiple cost drivers to allocate overhead.
In a JIT pull system, production is initiated only when there is actual demand, reducing inventory and waste.
Kanban is a visual signaling system used in JIT manufacturing to trigger production or movement of materials.
TQM emphasizes continuous improvement in all processes and a strong focus on customer satisfaction.
The product lifecycle consists of four stages: introduction, growth, maturity, and decline.
Cost estimation techniques include regression analysis, the high-low method, and account analysis, among others.
Account analysis classifies each account as fixed or variable based on managerial judgment and knowledge of cost behavior.
Engineering estimates derive costs from the physical relationships between inputs and outputs in the production process.
Cost of goods manufactured includes direct materials, direct labor, and applied manufacturing overhead.
Conversion costs are the costs required to convert raw materials into finished goods: direct labor plus manufacturing overhead.
Cost assignment involves tracing direct costs to cost objects and allocating indirect costs using allocation bases.

COSO Principle 14 requires the entity to internally communicate information necessary for internal control to function, including external communication.
Variables sampling is used to estimate numerical (dollar) values of a population, such as account balances.
Attributes sampling tests for the presence or absence of a specific characteristic, such as whether a control was applied.
The internal audit function should have unrestricted access to all records, personnel, and physical properties relevant to audits.
Pre-numbered documents are a control activity designed to ensure completeness and detect missing transactions.
Dual custody requires two individuals to be present when handling assets, reducing the risk of theft by any single individual.
Mandatory vacations are a detective control because another employee performs the duties and may uncover fraudulent activity.
Profit center performance is typically evaluated by comparing actual profit against budgeted profit.
Under ASC 280, segment disclosures must include segment profit or loss and segment assets at a minimum.
Budget vs actual variance analysis is primarily used for control purposes and to take corrective action on deviations.
A standard cost card specifies the standard price and standard quantity for each cost element (materials, labor, overhead).

Practical (currently attainable) standards allow for normal levels of downtime, waste, and other inefficiencies.

A revenue variance is favorable when actual revenue exceeds budgeted revenue.
